v2_findings.title: Cyber — Social Engineering / Cyber Deception Coverage
v2_findings.content:
[Ugly] Cyber — Social Engineering / Cyber Deception Coverage
Risk Score: 16/25

What this means:
You're a government vendor processing wires and ACH for county contracts. The most common cyberattack today — a fraudster sends a fake email pretending to be your CEO or a county official telling Accounts Payable to wire money — would not be covered by any policy in your program in any meaningful wa

Recommendation:
Restructure cyber deception terms at renewal: target $1M sublimit with $25K-$50K retention. If AmTrust won't restructure, market the cyber renewal — multiple carriers (Coalition, At-Bay, Beazley) offe

presentation_slides.title: Cyber Policy
body: You effectively have no coverage for Cyber Deception (cyber incident arising from social engineering)
They carved it out as a separate line item from a Cyber Event, gave you a $250k sublimit with a $250k deductible.

presentation_slides.title: Insufficient Cancellation Notice
body: We expect a 90-day notice of cancellation or nonrenewal from our carrier partners.
This gives us sufficient time to perform a thorough marketing effort for replacement coverage.

presentation_slides.title: Multiple Policies
body: Additional Named Insureds Completely or Partially Missing from most policies.

presentation_slides.title: Cyber Policy
body: Maricopa County asks for $5M limits, you have $4M.
This policy does NOT sit under any umbrella.
County also does not expressly state this can be secured through secondary excess policy.
